name: Bicycle wheel
line: A bicycle wheel. Click to spin it up.
shows: A road bicycle wheel: a black tread with tan sidewalls, an alloy rim with its valve, 24 spokes laced to a two-flange hub in the accent.
product: A wheel, a wheelset or a hub: the product of a maker of wheels or wheel parts. Never a whole bicycle: a wheel does not show a bike.
for: Wheels and wheel parts, cycling parts and service; on a software page, a card about motion, speed or a mechanism. A product page of site-kind other (a chair, a bike, a lamp, coffee) shows none: its photographs lead (MO-08); only a technical product (hardware) of that very kind may show it.
never: Never an object of another kind for a product, never on a place page or beside the client's own photographs, and never a print (halftone, engraving, dither, type) outside a software, tech, AI or games page. No caption under it: never call it a render, a drawing, an illustration, a model, a sample or made in code; the heading and text say what the product is. Its aria-label names the thing plainly (as label does).
motion: Sways through three-quarter views and rolls slowly on its axle.
hover: The light follows the pointer and the wheel leans toward it.
step: Click or Enter: the wheel spins up (at most about 220 degrees a second); click again to let it run down.

use.html: , then load assets/objects/_print-core/auto.js once (type="module", after system.js). auto.js mounts every [data-print].
use.js: import obj from '<assets>/objects/print-wheel/object.js'; const ctrl = obj.mount(el, { place: 'card' });
use.host: An empty element. In a .panel, .panel__screen or .frame it fills it (position absolute, inset 0) and prints over the panel's ground; anywhere else give it a size.

place.card: transparent over the panel's ground, large, cut by the bottom-left edge so the bottom-right corner stays clear for the pause button (an x.ai or Figma feature card); in a panel about as tall as wide (a phone) it is cut less. auto.js uses it for an object in a .panel.
place.tile: transparent, whole and standing low in a square .panel--top tile, the card's title and text under it. auto.js uses it in a .panel--top.
place.hero: transparent, large, right of centre in a wide .frame, the text in the clear left half; in a frame about as tall as wide (a phone) it sits smaller and low, under the text. auto.js uses it in a .frame.
place.none: outside a panel or frame: centred on its own paper (the demo page). data-print-place="none" asks for it anywhere.

params.effect: render (default: a studio render in its own materials) | halftone | engrave | dither | ascii (a print: software, tech, AI or games pages only)
params.size: 0.3..1.8, the share of the frame the object fills; over 1 it runs off the edges
params.turn: 1 turns by itself (and gets a pause button), 0 still until hovered or clicked
params.transparent: 1 prints over the ground (no paper of its own)
params.interactive: 0 a picture only: no hover, no click, not focusable
params.cell: CSS px of a cell, screen or line pitch (0: the print's own)

palette: From the panel's dealt ground (its data-fx-palette: the ground's paper, an ink that reads on it, the page accent), else the page tokens --bg, --surface, --ink, --accent; or data-print-palette / { palette } with bg, surface, ink, accent.
group: One object per card group turns (auto.js picks the first, or the one with data-print-loop); the others hold still until the pointer or a click moves them.
pause: A turning object puts its own round pause button (.loop-pause, 36px) in the bottom-right corner of its panel. Keep that corner clear.
reducedMotion: One still frame at the rest angle: no turn, no hover light, no pause button; a click shows the step at once.
keyboard: The object is a button (role button, aria-pressed for a toggle) with a focus ring inside the panel; Enter or Space takes the step.
cost: A WebGL2 context only while it moves near the screen; the objects of a page share 2. Raymarch at most 1 texel per CSS px while it moves (0.75 x 0.75 when large); a render at rest is drawn once at up to one texel per canvas pixel (1.2 megatexels at most), so the picture that stays is sharp; dither 1 texel per cell; a canvas never over 1.5 megapixels. A still object keeps its last frame as a plain picture.
fallback: Posters made by _print-core/make-fallbacks.html: fallback-render.png / fallback-render-dark.png (the render: plates left, colour right, the accent part relit in the page accent) and fallback.png / fallback-dark.png (print plates). The poster shows at once in the palette, cross-fades to the live picture, and stays when WebGL2 is missing, a shader is rejected or fails, or the first frame comes out empty.
